memo.verdict: Neutral; park, with a price trigger; conviction medium. The case is not invalidated. No gate parks it (management B, business quality B, predictability B, trackability B); the 'Modal return' parks it: an F at PLN 116.34 (about 4.2% a year over eighteen months, 7.0% a year over three years) that would be a B or better below about PLN 90 on the same path (PLN 82.5 clears 20% a year over three years; PLN 94.1 over eighteen months). Action: set the level and the two checks (clean net interest margin above 4.0%; CHF provisions below PLN 200 million a quarter) and wait. A Q3 2026 print on 5 November 2026 showing the margin holding above 4.1% while loans grow 13% would be the occasion to re-sort the case towards 'Compounder' and revisit the multiple applied.
case: - PKO is a cause-for-concern-clearing case that has already cleared. Poland's largest bank (a quarter of the loan market; cost-to-income near 30%; return on equity 18% to 19%) was masked for six years by Swiss franc provisions (PLN 24.3 billion since 2019; PLN 4.4 billion in 2025) and now reports almost clean (PLN 297 million in Q2 2026; coverage 188%; over 90% of contracts settled or in court; management expects immateriality by end-2026).

- The change is external and legal and has run its course; internal change is continuity. The chief executive (Szymon Midera, since 14 June 2024, 28 months before the memo date) and the "#1, full stop" strategy (24 October 2024: return on equity above 18% by 2027, cost-to-income below 35%, cost of risk 0.7% to 0.9%) are mature; guidance has been beaten every period since 2023 (+10.04%, +3.38%, +6.82%, +5.80% against guidance) but held, not raised. Internal forces C: one force at B (balance sheet: loans +13.5%, loan-to-deposit 66.2% from 64.4%, PLN 8.5 billion synthetic securitisation), standards B, new products B (Allegro Klik, PKO Pay Later 374 thousand customers), guidance raised D.

- External forces pull both ways (C). Demand B: GDP +4% in Q2 2026; investment projected +10% in 2026; EUR 137 billion of EU funds; consumer loans +21.5%, PLN mortgages +13.9%, corporate financing +15%; loans 32% of GDP against nearly 80% in the euro area; against, the consumer surge is partly non-recurring refinancing, the 2% Safe Mortgage subsidy expired, management guides mid-single digits. Political and regulatory D: corporate income tax 30% in 2026 from 19%, scheduled 26% (2027) and 23% (2028) with a sell-side-flagged risk the cuts do not come; reserve tax proposed (worst case 5% to 6% of 2026 net income, about PLN 350 million); election autumn 2027; reliefs from the CJEU WIBOR ruling (12 February 2026, C-471/24), the KNF long-term funding ratio cut to 20% from 40%, WIBOR phase-out postponed to 2036. Macro C: NBP paused at 3.75% (cut March 2026), CPI 4.0% (September 2026), houses split between hikes in 1Q27 and a terminal 3.25% by 3Q27 or 3.0% by end-2027; management guides 15 basis points of margin per 100 basis points of cuts and above 4% at a 3% rate. Own cycle C: volume up, margin down, revenue flat. Competition C (Santander Bank Polska mortgage rate cut from 15% to 9.5%; Erste's 49% stake intensifying corporate lending). Disruption B (BLIK 460.2 million transactions; over 80% of consumer decisions by machine learning; over 30% of new customers digital; Allegro Pay financing over 15% of platform GMV is the two-edged force). Supply B (deposits abundant; covered bond at mid-swaps plus 38 basis points). Catch-all C: the Polish sovereign (heavy holdings; Moody's cut PKO's covered bonds to Aa2).
counter_case: - At Building Block 1, the bull case at full strength: PKO is the best bank in a fast-growing, underpenetrated economy that is the main beneficiary of EUR 137 billion of EU funds. Loans grow 12% to 13% a year rather than 9%, because consumer credit is up 21.5%, corporate 15%, and the chief executive calls 2026 the strongest year in the bank's history. The clean margin rose 4 basis points in Q2 2026 while three-month WIBOR fell 174 basis points year on year, so the hedging works and the margin holds at 4.3%, not 4.1%. Costs fall year on year; the cost of risk is 29 to 31 basis points with unemployment at 3.1%; the CHF charge ends in 2026 and the tax rate falls seven points by 2028. The sell-side's 9% loan growth, 56 basis points of compression and 60% payout are three conservative assumptions stacked, so FY2028 earnings per share are PLN 13 or more rather than PLN 11.8, and a bank compounding earnings at 15% a year on a 19% return on equity deserves the eleven to twelve times the market pays for such banks; at PLN 13 of FY2028 earnings that is PLN 150 or more, the Morgan Stanley bull case of PLN 151. Conceded: the operating momentum is real and the beats consistent; 2.4 times book is not high for a 19% return on equity; consensus has been too low on volume for a year; if the margin holds at 4.3%, FY2028 earnings per share are about PLN 12.3 on our arithmetic (each 10 basis points of margin on about PLN 330 billion of loans is about PLN 330 million of net interest income, about PLN 0.19 of earnings per share after a 26% tax), and at 10.9 times that is about 15% a year, a C. Held: the bull case needs three things at once (margin holding, tax step-down arriving, multiple rising), each plausible or possible with low joint odds; the re-rating leg has been taken (6.9 times to 9.9 times in a year); the FY2027 step is tax and provisions, which investors do not extrapolate; the environment has turned against bank multiples through the sovereign-bank loop with Poland's sovereign under a Moody's downgrade. Where the bull wins: if the operating engine grows 10% a year rather than 6%, needing the margin to stop falling while loans grow 9%.

- At Building Block 2: the 'Foundations' are not robust because the owner is the foundation: a government that raised the sector's tax rate to 30% in one budget, legislated credit holidays twice, proposes a reserve tax, purged the board when the government changed and faces an election in autumn 2027; the margin is on the wrong side of its own rate cycle; the 15% to 20% state-ownership discount to mBank is the market's standing verdict; robustness C, and quality makes the bank a target for the fiscal authorities rather than a protection. Conceded in facts and direction; held at B because the test is whether the expected change is plausible and probable, and the operating change is modest, delivered through the worst CHF years, with courts and regulator lately ruling for the banks and the board professionalised. The owner can take a slice of the earnings; it has not shown it will stop the bank earning them.
triggers: - Price trigger: below about PLN 90 the modal path clears the bar (PLN 82.5 for 20% a year over three years; PLN 94.1 over eighteen months); at that level the 24-month-forward multiple would be 7.9 times our path.

- Margin: clean net interest margin above 4.1% in a quarter confirms; below 4.1% is the alarm; below 4.0% for two consecutive quarters invalidates (the earnings review's own invalidation); the NBP cutting through 3.0% invalidates. Watch three-month WIBOR daily, the NBP decision and CPI monthly. If the margin holds at 4.3% rather than 4.1%, FY2028 earnings per share rise to about PLN 12.3 and the 10.9 times branch gives about 15% a year.

- CHF run-off: quarterly provisions below PLN 200 million by Q4 2026 confirms; above PLN 200 million in Q4 2026 is the alarm; about PLN 0.4 billion in 2027 on our path (Morgan Stanley PLN 370 million).

- Loan growth and payout: Tier 1 below 14.00% is the alarm; a FY2026 dividend proposal below 60% of profit, or customer financing growth below 6% a year, would change our mind; a proposal at 50% is the bear case realised.

- Fiscal line: a budget proposal holding the corporate income tax rate at 30% or a reserve-remuneration cut proposed is the alarm; either enacted invalidates, taking 5% to 8% off FY2027 earnings in one announcement; the autumn 2027 election is the dated occasion.
- Cost of risk above 50 to 60 basis points for two consecutive quarters refutes the earnings path.
